issues.description: Behavioral change: s.state[k]=sorted now only runs when yield returns true, altering early-termination semantics
issues.detail: Previously the sorted marker was set unconditionally after pop; now it only fires inside the yield-true branch. The deferred clear papers over the difference, but the changed postcondition on early yield=false is undocumented and unjustified in the commit message. State the new postcondition explicitly.

issues.description: No regression test for the state-reuse bug the PR claims to fix
issues.detail: The PR's stated purpose is fixing Sorter state reuse, yet no test calls Sort twice on the same Sorter and asserts results plus len(s.stack)==0 and len(s.state)==0 afterward. Without a regression test the fix can be silently reverted by future refactors. Add the test.

issues.description: Sorter reuse contract and state-machine invariant are unwritten
issues.detail: Collapsing working and walking into one state is the right simplification, but no invariant distinguishes first from second visit, no termination argument is given, and no precondition/postcondition is stated for Sorter reuse, reentrancy panic, or early-yield abandonment. Write a short spec comment on the Sorter type covering the state machine and reuse semantics.

issues.description: Three independent fixes squashed into one diff
issues.detail: The patch bundles (1) collapsing working/walking, (2) fixing s.stack[0:] to clear()+s.stack[:0], and (3) moving the sorted marker inside the yield branch. Each is a distinct bug with distinct reasoning; squashing them defeats bisect and complicates review. Split into separate commits.

issues.description: New comment contains typos 'visisted' and 'if its' in load-bearing documentation
issues.detail: The updated comment is the de-facto spec for the state field after the working/walking collapse. 'visisted' should be 'visited' and 'if its' should be 'if it's'. Typos in correctness-critical documentation invite readers to skim past it. Tighten the prose.

issues.description: Moving cleanup to defer changes when stale state is purged versus original entry-time clear
issues.detail: Original code cleared state on entry to Sort; the new code clears in a defer installed after the reentrancy panic check. If the returned iter.Seq is never invoked, prior state persists. The defer is defensive-as-substitute for an explicit entry precondition. State the precondition or restore entry-time clearing.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the underlying fixes are real and the working/walking collapse is the right simplification, but the patch is presented as a bug-fix without the discipline such a fix requires. Three independent changes are squashed into one diff, the sorted-marker now fires only on yield=true (a quiet semantic change), and no regression test exercises the Sorter-reuse contract the PR claims to repair. The Sorter's state machine and reuse precondition/postcondition are nowhere written down, and the new comment that should serve as the spec contains typos. Verdict: needs work — split the commits, document the invariant and reuse contract, fix the comment, and add a Sort-twice regression test before landing.
